Effects of a policy adopted at different times

Source: R/stgdid.R
stgdid.Rd

Difference-in-differences estimators for staggered adoption that never use an already-treated unit as a control: the group-time effects of Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021), optionally with covariates; the regression on cohort-period cells of Wooldridge (2021); and, for a treatment that switches on and off, the estimator of de Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2020) with its placebo. Standard errors come from the cluster bootstrap.

Usage

stgdid(
  y,
  unit,
  time,
  first = NULL,
  trt = NULL,
  meth = "csa",
  ctrl = "notyet",
  adj = NULL,
  est = "dr",
  clus = NULL,
  reps = 499,
  seed = NULL,
  level = 0.95
)

Arguments

y

The outcome: finite numbers, one per row (counts from 0 for fam = "pois" or "nb").

unit

The unit of each row: labels.

time

The period of each row: numbers (a year, a month index); each unit at most once per period.

first

The period each row's unit is first treated (constant within units; NA, 0 or Inf for never), or NULL with trt.

trt

The treatment of each row, 0 or 1, or NULL with first. For meth = "csa" and "wool" it must stay on once on.

meth

"csa", "wool" or "dcdh".

ctrl

"notyet" or "never": the comparison units of "csa".

adj

NULL or covariates for "csa": a data frame or list of columns, a numeric matrix or one vector, one value per row.

est

With adj: "dr", "ipw" or "reg".

clus

NULL (resample units) or the cluster of each row, constant within units.

reps

The bootstrap samples: a whole number from 0 (no standard errors).

seed

The seed of the bootstrap: NULL to draw it from R's generator (so set.seed() fixes it), or a whole number from 0.

level

The confidence level of the intervals: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

Value

An object of class stgdid, a list: att, the group-time effects (cohort, period, evtm, est, se, lo, hi, ncoh the cohort's size; NULL for "dcdh"); overall (term, est, se, lo, hi, and for "dcdh" the rows "effect" and "placebo" with n, the switchers); dynamic, by event time (evtm, est, se, lo, hi; NULL for "dcdh"); meth; ctrl; reps; and level.

Details

Let cohort g be the units first treated in period g, and the comparison units those never treated (ctrl = "never") or not yet treated by period max(t, b) ("notyet", outside cohort g). For meth = "csa", ATT(g, t) is the cohort's mean change in the outcome from the base period b less the comparison units', with b = g - 1 from adoption on and b = t - 1 before (the "varying" base of the 'did' package), so an effect before adoption is a placebo over one period. With adj, parallel trends need hold only given the covariates, taken at the base period, and each cell is the estimator of Sant'Anna and Zhao (2020) on the cohort and its comparison units: "dr", the doubly robust mean_D(dy - m(x)) - sum w (dy - m(x)) / sum w with m the least-squares fit of the change among the comparison units and w = p / (1 - p) from the logistic propensity p of belonging to the cohort; "ipw" without m; "reg" without the weights. Comparison units with p of 0.995 or more are left out, as 'DRDID' does. Use covariates fixed before treatment.

For meth = "wool", the regression of the outcome on unit and period effects and one indicator for every treated cohort-period cell gives each ATT(g, t) after adoption as a coefficient (without covariates this is the imputation estimator); without units never treated, the periods from the last adoption on are left out.

The overall effect averages the ATT(g, t) after adoption weighted by cohort size (the "simple" aggregation of 'did'); the effect at event time e averages ATT(g, g + e) over the cohorts observed at e, weighted by cohort size. Event time counts observed periods. Units treated from the first period are left out.

For meth = "dcdh", in each period the units that switch into treatment are compared with the units untreated in both periods, and the units that switch out with the units treated in both: DID_M = sum_t (N_join,t DID_join,t + N_leave,t DID_leave,t) / N_S over the N_S switchers that have a comparison. The placebo runs the same comparison one period earlier, for units whose treatment did not change over the two periods before; it should be near zero.

Standard errors are the standard deviations over reps bootstrap samples of the clusters (units by default), drawn with replacement, with everything recomputed; intervals are normal.

References

Callaway, B. and Sant'Anna, P. H. C. (2021). Difference-in-differences with multiple time periods. Journal of Econometrics, 225(2), 200-230. doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.12.001

Sant'Anna, P. H. C. and Zhao, J. (2020). Doubly robust difference-in-differences estimators. Journal of Econometrics, 219(1), 101-122. doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.06.003

Wooldridge, J. M. (2021). Two-way fixed effects, the two-way Mundlak regression, and difference-in-differences estimators. doi:10.2139/ssrn.3906345

de Chaisemartin, C. and D'Haultfoeuille, X. (2020). Two-way fixed effects estimators with heterogeneous treatment effects. American Economic Review, 110(9), 2964-2996. doi:10.1257/aer.20181169

Examples

d <- expand.grid(year = 2015:2024, town = LETTERS[1:12])
i <- match(d$town, LETTERS)
d$first <- c(2019, 2019, 2019, 2019, 2021, 2021, 2021, 2021,
             NA, NA, NA, NA)[i]
on <- !is.na(d$first) & d$year >= d$first
d$rate <- 30 + i + 0.5 * (d$year - 2015) - 4 * on + sin(seq_len(120))
s <- stgdid(d$rate, d$town, d$year, d$first, reps = 99, seed = 1)
s$overall
#>   term       est        se        lo        hi
#> 1  att -4.034678 0.4943916 -5.003667 -3.065688
s$dynamic
#>    evtm         est        se         lo         hi
#> 1    -5 -0.37997631 0.3609287 -1.0873837  0.3274310
#> 2    -4 -0.22087536 0.4097379 -1.0239469  0.5821962
#> 3    -3  0.17184724 0.3162810 -0.4480521  0.7917466
#> 4    -2  0.12208141 0.3516011 -0.5670441  0.8112069
#> 5    -1  0.03901677 0.3476043 -0.6422751  0.7203086
#> 6     0 -4.07991970 0.3376486 -4.7416987 -3.4181407
#> 7     1 -4.20529807 0.6010068 -5.3832497 -3.0273464
#> 8     2 -4.06033981 0.7271590 -5.4855453 -2.6351344
#> 9     3 -4.07107236 0.6724557 -5.3890612 -2.7530835
#> 10    4 -3.58751419 0.6612129 -4.8834677 -2.2915606
#> 11    5 -3.92600168 0.1549628 -4.2297231 -3.6222803
# a by-law some towns repeal
d$law <- as.integer(on & !(i == 1 & d$year >= 2022))
stgdid(d$rate, d$town, d$year, trt = d$law, meth = "dcdh", reps = 49,
       seed = 1)$overall
#>      term        est        se         lo         hi n
#> 1  effect -3.6698465 0.4276516 -4.5080282 -2.8316647 9
#> 2 placebo -0.0742311 0.3569557 -0.7738514  0.6253892 9
